purpose: Same-runner, same-image interleaved comparison of automatic source-format down-holds
scope: Direct WebRTC on an isolated Docker bridge, without tunnel, TURN, MediaMTX, authentication or physical capture. All six attempts use one hosted runner and identical image digests.

All six format ladders and source-target recoveries pass. All six original playback and viewer recovery verdicts fail and remain failed. The sixth trial also misses exact first-presentation measurement (presentedFrames is two).

The legacy four-second steady interval subtracts the preceding one-second snapshot. Every failed steady freeze increment includes an interval starting near three seconds and ending near four seconds; it does not prove that the increment occurred after four seconds.

Browser frame gaps and native freeze increments are separate observations. Correlation does not independently reproduce the browser native freeze classifier. Both raw intervals and browser-clock frame events are retained below.

Phase-relative browser diagnostics are relative to the first observed phase snapshot, not the exact network-shaping activation. The host phase marker has only whole-second precision, including in the earlier 18338c8 comparison.

Total transition freeze durations overlap between one- and three-second down-holds. No production timing, acceptance budget or historical verdict is changed. A bounded native-counter boundary measurement is required before selecting a timing policy.
Baseline and recovery native freeze counters remain unchanged in all six attempts. Measurements concern these synthetic sources and this environment, not target-device performance.
